title: Fast-Iter Bench Tally (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tally for small iterative experiments — capture enough numbers to decide whether to promote a config to CI-level runs. Not a polished doc; shortcuts, TODOs and mvp stats only.

Legend / columns I keep: date | model | quant | hw | batch | seq | effective_toks/s | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes

-- raw entries (most-recent first) --
2026-03-08 | gptx-7b-fp16 | fp16 | a100-40 | 8 | 512 | 14300 | 68 | 210 | 0.012 | small plateau at steady state, KV cache warm after 3 requests
2026-03-02 | gptx-7b-q4_0 | q4_0 | a10x | 16 | 256 | 9800 | 92 | 330 | 0.006 | big cost win, p95 jitter high when seq>256
2026-02-26 | gptx-13b-fp16 | fp16 | a100-80 | 4 | 1024 | 27000 | 54 | 160 | 0.027 | throughput strong but startup cost high, consider batching policy change
2026-02-10 | gptx-7b-fp16 | fp16 | a10x | 32 | 128 | 6200 | 120 | 410 | 0.015 | noisy on a10x, preemption events maybe
2026-01-21 | gptx-7b-q4_1 | q4_1 | a100-40 | 12 | 256 | 11200 | 75 | 240 | 0.007 | q4_1 stable, slightly worse quality than fp16 on long tails

Rapid observations:
- a100-family gives predictable p95; a10x cheaper but flaky p95 and occasional preemption ~= noisy variance.
- q4 quant gives ~45-55% token cost reduction but watch p95 tail. Good for non-critical background tasks.
- Batch size sweet spot depends heavily on seq length distribution; for median seq ~200, batch 12-16 seems decent.

Quick cost calc (hand math):
- cost_per_1k_tokens = (instance_hourly_usd / (effective_toks_per_sec * 3600)) * 1000  // rough
- Example: a100-40 @ $4.00/hr, effective 14,300 toks/s -> cost ~ (4 / (14300*3600))*1000 = ~0.000077 -> multiply by any infra multipliers (network, infra overhead) to match billing. I use a fudge x150 in tracker -> ~0.012 shown above.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Formalize batching policy experiment matrix (batch sizes x seq buckets) and push to GH issue (blocking: time to provision uniform instances).
- [x] Re-run gptx-7b-q4_0 with a100-40 to confirm p95 is hardware-bound (done 2026-03-02).
- [ ] Add micro-eval prompt set to check quality delta q4_0 vs fp16 for >512 tokens.
- [ ] Try persistent KV cache warm strategy (pin small cache on same instance across calls) to reduce startup p50.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- For CI promotion require: p95 < 300ms on target infra OR fallback route to cheaper model with <2x latency and documented quality regression.
- Consider adding small synthetic load test that spikes to 2x traffic for 90s to surface p95 tails before rollout.
- Keep one-line summary per experiment: e.g., "q4_0 on a100-40 == cost win, tail risk for long sequences" and add to ticket title.

Unresolved questions:
- How to map effective_toks/s in these quick runs to Redwood billing (tokenization differences)? Leave margin.
- Is preemption on a10x caused by noisy neighbor or our autoscaler? Need SRE check (raise JIRA).

Scratch formulas I type often: 
- seconds_per_1k_toks = 1000 / toks_per_sec
- cost_per_1k = instance_hourly / (3600 / seconds_per_1k_toks) // same as above but often easier in head

Short raw checklist for next run: provision a100-40, model gptx-7b-q4_0, batch sizes [8,12,16], seq buckets [<=128, 129-512, >512], capture p50/p95/throughput+cpu mem, tag run id in GH-PR-4821.
